extracted.intended_audience: researchers in xenotransplantation, transplant immunology, genetic engineering, and translational/preclinical scientists
extracted.subtask_description: Design, engineering, in vitro validation, and nonhuman-primate (NHP) preclinical testing of genetically engineered porcine renal donors for clinical xenotransplantation. Covers genomic edits, transgene selection, functional assays, transplantation procedure, pathology scoring and reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinically ready porcine donor — composite design requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A clinically ready porcine donor must be engineered and its xenograft successfully tested in a nonhuman primate model to assess safety and efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should address molecular incompatibilities (cell-surface glycan antigens, complement, coagulation and inflammation regulators) and zoonotic risk (PERV). The donor should combine glycan knockouts, human transgene expression and PERV inactivation as needed to approach human compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of major porcine glycan antigens (3KO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Porcine cells display three major glycan antigens — α-Gal, Neu5Gc and Sd(a) — produced by GGTA1, CMAH and B4GALNT2/B4GALNT2L genes; a human-compatible donor should ideally have all three glycans eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3KO (knockouts of GGTA1, CMAH, B4GALNT2/B4GALNT2L) reduces preformed antibody binding and complement activation. Expect residual antigenicity and possible additional xenoantigens; verify phenotype by IHC and glycan-detection reagents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human transgene selection and function (7TG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of human genes that mitigate complement, coagulation, innate immunity and inflammation: CD46, CD55 (complement), THBD, PROCR (coagulation), CD47 (innate immunity), TNFAIP3 and HMOX1 (anti-apoptotic/anti-inflammatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design transgene constructs (polycistronic with 2A sequences, multiple promoters) to achieve durable, cell-type-appropriate expression. Test individual contributions (e.g., block CD46 or CD55) to confirm functional activity. Include redundancy (both CD46 and CD55) to resist loss by shedding/cleavage.

rubrics_metrics.name: PERV (porcine endogenous retrovirus) inactivation (RI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inactivate PERV sequences (many copies present) to mitigate zoonotic risk because PERV transmission to human cells in culture has been demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify inactivation across all copies (e.g., by sequencing); consider RI (retroviral inactivation) as a separate genotype dimension (3KO.RI, 3KO.7TG.RI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pig breed and blood-type selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose pig breed and blood type appropriate for clinical translation: Yucatan miniature pig chosen because organ sizes are comparable to human organs; OO blood type was selected to eliminate ABO incompatibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breed selection should consider organ size, physiology and husbandry. Blood-type selection avoids ABO mismatch complications in transplantation studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genome-editing strategy and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CRISPR–Cas9-mediated NHEJ/HDR and recombinase-mediated cassette exchange to introduce multiple edits and transgene payloads; document number and nature of edits (example: 69 genomic edits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform stepwise editing/cloning and verify edits after each round. Provide detailed maps of edits and inserted constructs (Extended Data/Figures and Supplementary Tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbour insertion of transgene payload
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert transgenic construct (Payload 15S / PL15S) hemizygously into a genomic safe-harbour (AAVS1 orthologous site, PPP1R12C) to reduce insertional mutagenesis risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm insertion locus, copy number and intactness by long-read sequencing and alignment to a custom chromosome containing the payload; report whether insertion is intronic/exonic and any disruption of endogenous genes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genotype verification by sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify 3KO, 7TG and RI genotypes by sequencing: long-read whole-genome sequencing, PCR sequencing of CRISPR target sites, and NGS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sequencing coverage, allelic states for each target, and any rearrangements (e.g., rearranged payloads). Exclude or annotate animals with compromised payload sequences from group analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transgene expression confirmation and durability
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate transcription and protein expression of all transgenes by direct RNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, IHC and western blot; show expression in contralateral donor kidney and persistence in graft at necropsy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report promoter-specific expression (e.g., CAG, ssUBC, ssEEF1A1) and relative expression across cell types (endothelial, fenestrated ECs, glomerular ECs). Quantify and provide images for cross-time durability (e.g., expression at transplant and at necropsy day 176).

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro functional endothelial assays — antibody binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure binding of primate/human IgG and IgM to porcine endothelial cells to assess preformed antibody recognition (e.g., using 96 cynomolgus sera).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run technical and biological replicates, compare WT vs 3KO vs 3KO.7TG cells, and include human controls. Use statistical tests (Wilcoxon matched-pairs, Student's t-tests) and report residual binding levels and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro complement activation assays (C3b deposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess complement activation by measuring surface-bound C3b deposition after incubation in human or NHP serum; compare porcine KECs to human endothelial cells (HUVECs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that reduced deposition on 3KO relative to WT may still be substantial; demonstrate further reduction with human transgene expression. Include EDTA controls and dashed-line baselines for EDTA-treated serum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement-dependent cytotoxicity and cell lysis assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Test complement-dependent cytotoxicity over varying incubation times (e.g., up to 15 h) to evaluate protection provided by 3KO and by 3KO.7TG ± RI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report time-dependence; 3KO may protect against short incubations with human serum but not long-term; 3KO.7TG ± RI should provide greater protection for both human and cynomolgus serum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coagulation regulation assays — aPC production and TAT formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess aPC generation in presence of human thrombin and protein C, and measure thrombin–antithrombin (TAT) formation and whole-blood clotting to test compatibility of thrombomodulin and EPCR transgenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that WT/3KO porcine cells do not produce aPC but 3KO.7TG ± RI do; use blocking antibodies to parse contributions of EPCR and thrombomodulin; report reductions in TAT and whole-blood coagulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional validation of specific transgenes via blocking/overexpression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use blocking antibodies and expression/overexpression constructs for individual transgenes (e.g., CD46, CD55, EPCR, TM, CD47, TNFAIP3, HMOX1) to verify their functional contribution to complement regulation, coagulation, SIRPα signalling, and anti-apoptotic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include controls (empty vector, isotype), dose–response (e.g., anti-hCD47 mAb titration), and confirm outcomes (C3b reduction, aPC production, SIRPα reporter activation, reduced caspase 3/7 activation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apoptosis/inflammation resilience assays (TNFAIP3, HMOX1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess protection from TNF-induced apoptosis using caspase 3/7 activation assays in cells expressing TNFAIP3 and/or HMOX1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report individual and combined effects; include western blot confirmation of expression and technical replicate data showing reduced caspase activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking to human endothelial cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare porcine engineered-cell functional readouts to human endothelial cell controls (HUVECs, human glomerular microvascular ECs) to demonstrate human‑level compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include directly comparable assays (aPC production, C3b deposition, coagulation) and report when engineered porcine cells are indistinguishable from human cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHP recipient screening and pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: Screen NHP recipients for porcine-reactive preformed antibody binding and preferentially select monkeys with lower antibody binding to 3KO AECs/KECs for transplantation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize practical constraints: NHP availability and cost may prevent statistically powered allocation; pairing is often empirical and dictated by availability. Report selection criteria and any pre-screening thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunosuppression regimen for NHP transplants
rubrics_metrics.description: Use induction therapy with B and T lymphocyte depletion, maintenance therapy with anti-CD154 antibody and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), and a brief post-transplant course of tacrolimus and steroids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document dosing, timing and any deviations. Note that failures (dnDSA, TMA, AMR) may arise over time even with this regimen; use regimen data to inform clinical protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgical/transplant procedure and nephrectomy approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Transplant a genetically engineered porcine kidney concurrently with bilateral native nephrectomy of the recipient; document any variations (e.g., unilateral native nephrectomy with later contralateral nephrectomy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report perioperative management and any surgical complications. Note that unilateral nephrectomy variations and procedural differences should be recorded and considered in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia and study endpoint criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Define renal failure and humane end-point criteria: renal failure based on multiple creatinine >6–8 mg dl−1 and/or BUN >100 mg dl−1 unless otherwise noted; renal insufficiency defined as creatinine 3–6 mg dl−1 and/or BUN 60–100 mg dl−1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these biochemical thresholds in combination with clinical symptomatology to determine humane end points; report exact criteria applied to each animal and reasons for euthanasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Histopathology and rejection assessment — Banff-adapted criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess rejection by histopathology using the Banff classification of renal allograft pathology with modifications adapted for xenotransplantation (xenotransplantation-adapted criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score for AMR, TMA, ATI, TCMR, CAMR and annotate atypical features (e.g., species coagulation incompatibilities). Use C4d staining interpretation (C4d positivity may be expected upstream of CD46/CD55) and provide representative photomicrographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring donor-specific antibodies (DSA/dnDSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure donor-specific antibody (IgM/IgG) in peripheral blood over time and report presence/absence and kinetics of de novo DSA (dnDSA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlate dnDSA with pathology (AMR, TMA) and clinical events (infections, biopsies) that might trigger humoral responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kidney function metrics and clinical lab monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor kidney function via measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR), serum creatinine, serum albumin, serum potassium and blood platelet counts; interpret abnormalities in context of graft function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present longitudinal lab data, indicate normal ranges, and relate abrupt changes to graft failure or other complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design, replication, randomization and blinding reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sample-size rationale (e.g., no a priori power calculation due to NHP constraints), replication (independent experiments/sites), randomization procedures, blinding status and data exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about practical limitations: NHP studies may be empirically determined and not blinded; document any excluded transplants (e.g., those with payload rearrangements) and rationale for pooling genotype groups for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of reagents and antibodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate antibodies and detection reagents for cross-reactivity and specificity (e.g., antibodies developed to recognize human orthologs were validated to not cross-react with porcine proteins; glycan reagents validated by positive staining of WT porcine tissues and absence in knockout tissues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vendor/catalog numbers and validation approaches (flow cytometry/IHC/western blot controls). For reagents known to cross-react with NHP, document reasoned acceptance (e.g., anti-CD154 clones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell line and primary cell reporting and authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sources of primary porcine cells and human cell lines, perform authentication (NGS confirmation of porcine donor genotypes; flow cytometry verification for human lines), and report mycoplasma testing status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include catalog numbers for purchased lines, describe derivation for primary cells, and disclose whether mycoplasma testing was performed; highlight any limitations (primary porcine cells not routinely mycoplasma-tested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow cytometry reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide axis labels with marker and fluorochrome, contour/pseudocolor plots, numerical values for cell percentages (with statistics), instrument and software details, and gating strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List instrument models, acquisition software, gating steps (FSC/SSC, singlets, live/dead, CD31 for ECs) and provide exemplar gating figures in Supplementary Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics oversight and animal welfare compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain and report IACUC approvals for all animal procedures (provide protocol numbers), adhere to NIH Guidelines and the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, and follow 3R principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify institutional approvals for each site, and document housing, surgical and postoperative care standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting transparency — Reporting Summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow journal reporting summary guidelines: disclose sample size decisions, data exclusions, replication, randomization, blinding, sex/gender reporting and population characteristics where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sex/gender, indicate whether considered in study design, how determined, and provide disaggregated source data if collected. For race/ethnicity/other social groupings, provide definitions and classification methods when applicable to human studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of xenotransplantation-adapted pathology criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Because xenotransplant rejection mechanisms can differ from allotransplantation, adapt histopathological scoring to include features important in xenotransplantation (e.g., antibody-mediated microangiopathy driven by complement or coagulation incompatibility even without dnDSA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the adapted scoring table (Extended Data Table and Supplementary Tables) and explain differences from standard Banff criteria; use this adapted system for informative diagnosis in xenotransplantation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and adverse-event monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor for and report clinical adverse events (infections, epistaxis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, respiratory insufficiency, oedema, hemoptysis) and link to graft pathologies (TMA, AMR) and interventions (biopsies, immunosuppression changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document causal inferences carefully: infections or biopsies may trigger immune responses leading to graft injury; provide timelines and contextual lab/pathology correlations.
